 'Serving this state is a calling for me," Comer said on Monday night
 By
 Elizabeth Elkind Fox News

 close Video Rep James Comer says Democrats will try to ‘ruin’ those in proximity to Trump administration 
 House Oversight Committee chairman Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., discusses Democrats’ intention to pursue legal action against President Donald Trump and his allies on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., is launching a campaign for governor on Monday night.
 "Serving this state is a calling for me," Comer said during a tele-townhall. "Kentucky needs a leader whose policies will lead to growth and good-paying jobs. We need a leader whose priority will be to reduce taxes so Kentuckians can keep more of what they earn."
 Comer teased a "major announcement" for Monday night earlier in the day. A source familiar with his plans told Fox News Digital it would be his long-awaited campaign to lead the commonwealth of Kentucky.
 REDISTRICTING EFFORTS BLOW UP IN REPUBLICANS' FACES AMID HISTORIC HOUSE LOSSES 
 House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., speaks at a press conference at the U.S. Capitol on Oct. 21, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images) 
 Comer spent the majority of his announcement fielding questions from Kentuckians on topics like education, small business, and high prices.
 Among the policies he advocated for was reducing Kentucky's income tax to zero.
 "We all talk about attracting new businesses and new industry to Kentucky," Comer said. "If we can get that existing income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state and help our state grow into the future."
 Kentucky's gubernatorial election will take place in November 2027, with the primaries set for May of that year.
 Gov. Andy Beshear, who is widely considered a potential contender for the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, is term-limited.
 Andy Beshear, governor of Kentucky, speaks during a campaign event with Rob Sand, then-Democratic gubernatorial candidate for Iowa, not pictured, at The River Center in Des Moines, Iowa, US, on Sunday, June 7, 2026. (KC McGinnis/Bloomberg via Getty Images) 
 Comer ran for Kentucky governor in 2015 but narrowly lost the GOP primary to former Gov. Matt Bevin.
 But this election cycle will likely see the House lawmaker enter as the frontrunner for his party's nomination.
 Comer has served in the House of Representatives since November 2016, when he won a special election for Kentucky's 1st congressional district. Since then, his profile has skyrocketed as the top Republican on the House Oversight Committee for the better part of the last six years.
 FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE 
 As committee chairman since Republicans took back the House majority in 2023, he's launched investigations into former President Joe Biden's use of autopen and the federal government's handling of Jeffrey Epstein's case, among others.
 Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., chairman of the House Oversight and Accountability Committee, left, and Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, attend a hearing in Washington, D.C., on March 4, 2026. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg/Getty Images)

 And despite Beshear's popularity as the state's two-term Democratic governor, Kentucky has historically been seen as a red state.
 President Donald Trump defeated former Vice President Kamala Harris by roughly 30 points there in 2024. He beat former President Joe Biden there by 25.9% in 2020.
 Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.
